links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: The token is, in the issuer's own words, 'a non-negotiable digital record evidencing a pro rata beneficial entitlement (if any)' as beneficiary of a BVI bare trust over a pooled holding of the referenced shares — with no entitlement to any specific identifiable share. Crucially, the trustee recognises only Trek Forge Ltd (a Backpack affiliate) as Tokenholder and sole beneficiary; a person holding the token in their own wallet 'becomes the on-chain holder of those Tokens for blockchain transfer purposes only' and has no redemption, distribution, instruction or enforcement right against the trust unless and until a 'Direct Redemption Contingency' occurs (Backpack insolvency, cessation, >90 days of suspended redemptions, court order, etc.) and the trustee expressly registers them. In practice a holder realises value by depositing the token back into a KYC'd Backpack Exchange account, which burns it and credits an off-chain UCC Article 8 security entitlement.

Real SpaceX shares are held through regulated US brokerage infrastructure in an OMNIBUS account at RQD Clearing, LLC (Clearing Broker; SEC-registered, FINRA & SIPC member, CRD 134284 / SEC 8-66826), with Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC as Intermediary Broker (CRD 317194 / SEC 8-70868). Under the Issuer T&C the Underlying Assets are held by Trek Nexus Markets Ltd 'as legal owner or holder of record and as bare trustee', and the trustee 'may hold Underlying Assets and proceeds in omnibus or commingled accounts' (commingled only within the same Approved Asset pool) while simultaneously stating it 'does not act as a commercial custodian or administrator' and may appoint unnamed regulated custodians. NO custodian for the tokenized pool is named in any document, and how the BVI bare trust's legal title sits alongside the RQD/Atomic Vaults account chain is undocumented. SIPC: the Brokerage ToS states that stocks are held in the Omnibus Account and 'only the Omnibus Account will receive SIPC coverage', which 'may therefore be shared among all Users and may be insufficient'; and expressly 'The Tokens are not insured or guaranteed by SIPC, any deposit insurance scheme, or any governmental agency.'

links.label: Issuance and redemption

fields.value: Practically: any user with a KYC-verified Backpack Exchange account in a supported region (not US/UK/UAE/Japan, not Backpack EU) can deposit the token and have it converted into a traditional securities holding. Legally: only Trek Forge Ltd (or its nominee/custodian) may submit a redemption request to the trustee; 'on-chain holders and holders of Exchange Account Entitlements have no entitlement to access Redemption or burning functionalities in the ordinary course' (cl. 4.1(a)). Direct redemption against the trustee is available only after a Direct Redemption Contingency and then only subject to the trustee's KYC/KYT, proof of entitlement and express register update. No Prohibited Person or U.S. person may be registered as beneficiary or exercise redemption (cl. 4.1(c)).

Deposit the token from a Solana wallet into a Backpack Exchange account; the token is burned and the position becomes a traditional securities holding (a UCC Article 8 security entitlement) in the same account. The trustee's mechanics are: lock the tokens, burn them, then either transfer the pro rata portion of the pooled shares or — at the trustee's determination — sell them and relay the net cash proceeds ('Redemption Relay', cl. 4.2(iii)-(iv), cl. 4.6), so share delivery is not guaranteed. Onward movement to an outside broker is described as 'ACATS- and DTCC-eligible via the brokerage infrastructure', but Backpack's own support docs state plainly that 'ACATS transfers to other brokerages are still being worked on and are not currently available' and 'Support for external broker-to-broker stock transfers is still under development and is not yet available'.

Withdrawal of a tokenized security from Backpack Exchange to Solana: an estimated platform fee of approximately $0.50, paid in the tokenized security being withdrawn, with no additional fees. Deposits (token to traditional securities): no Backpack fee, holder pays the Solana network fee. Stock trading: no separate commission or platform fee; the quoted price is the traded price. Transaction Costs of a redemption are borne by the holder and netted from proceeds; the trustee may also set off amounts owing.

From Backpack's own asset API (https://api.backpack.exchange/api/v1/assets): minimumDeposit 0.004 SPCX, minimumWithdrawal 0.008 SPCX, withdrawalFee 0.004 SPCX. On the brokerage leg every stock order must be worth at least $1; fractional to 0.01 share during regular hours, whole shares only outside them.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: For the token: dividends received on the pool are applied by the trustee 'to the acquisition of additional units of such Approved Asset (net of any applicable fees, expenses, or withholdings)' (cl. 3.7), and Backpack describes this as automatic reinvestment into additional tokenized shares with corporate actions reflected through 'proportional token balance adjustments designed to maintain economic equivalence'. The mint carries the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension for exactly that, though its multiplier was still 1 on 2026-09-16 (SpaceX pays no dividend). Voting: cl. 3.9 has the trustee exercise voting only on instructions from the registered Tokenholder — i.e. Trek Forge — so an on-chain holder has no voting channel; and on the off-chain brokerage side Backpack's own status table lists voting rights, cash dividend payouts, and splits/corporate actions reflected in balances as all 'still being worked on', not enabled.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: The token side is unregulated and says so: 'The Company and the Tokens are not registered with, endorsed, or approved by the British Virgin Islands Financial Services Commission or any other regulatory authority', and the issuer asserts the Tokens 'do not constitute securities, certificates representing investments, depositary receipts, notes, collective investment scheme units, rights or interests in investments or other regulated investments as defined under the Securities and Investment Business Act (SIBA)'. The Risk Disclosure adds that Tokens 'are not designed or marketed as an investment product' and that nothing 'shall constitute an offer of securities or an investment, or be deemed to create an investment contract in any jurisdiction'. The distribution basis is Regulation S: the Asset Tokenization ToS states the Tokens 'have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933 ... [and] may not be offered or sold in the United States or to US persons'. Regulated status sits one layer down, in the custody chain: RQD Clearing, LLC (Clearing Broker, CRD 134284 / SEC 8-66826) and Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC (Intermediary Broker, CRD 317194 / SEC 8-70868, formerly Olympus Mons Securities, LLC — note Backpack's docs spell it 'Atomic Vault' singular), both SEC-registered broker-dealers and FINRA & SIPC members. VERIFIED NEGATIVE: FINRA BrokerCheck firm search and SEC IAPD return zero records for 'Backpack', 'Backpack Securities', 'Trek Labs', 'Trek Nexus' and 'Trek Forge'; there is no CRD number, Form BD or SEC registration for any Backpack or Trek entity. SEC EDGAR full-text search returns no Backpack/Trek filings (the six hits for 'Backpack Securities' are unrelated third parties) and no Form D, Reg A or registration statement for SPCX. The consumer-facing introducing broker, Backpack Securities Global Limited, is a New Zealand corporation serving 'non-U.S. customers'. The widely repeated press description of SPCX as issued by 'a regulated U.S. broker-dealer' is therefore not supported by any primary document. Backpack Securities is NOT available to users in the United States, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates or Japan, and is not offered on Backpack EU; cl. 4.1(b) prohibits transferring the token to or for the benefit of any U.S. person. Mark Wetjen (former CFTC Acting Chairman) was appointed President of 'Backpack US' around 2026-03-05, which signals a US expansion effort but is not itself a registration. STRONGEST NEGATIVE: Backpack's own 'US Licenses, Registrations, and Regulatory Disclosures' page, stated as current 'As of September 2026', discloses only money transmission — FinCEN MSB registration 31000329581307 for Trek Labs, Inc., NMLS ID 2665675, plus state money-transmitter licences (Delaware 042857, DC MTR2665675, Iowa 2025-0047 and others) — and contains zero occurrences of 'broker-dealer', 'FINRA', 'SEC' or 'Securities and Exchange'. That is the page a US broker-dealer registration would appear on. Separately, the Brokerage ToS says Backpack Securities Global Limited 'acts solely in its capacities as custodian of Stocks and as a Securities Intermediary'. Sector-wide regulator position: the SEC Division of Corporation Finance staff statement on tokenized securities (2026-01-28) distinguishes securities tokenized by or on behalf of the issuer from those tokenized by unaffiliated third parties, and holds that 'the format in which a security is issued or the methods by which holders are recorded (e.g., onchain vs. offchain) does not affect application of the federal securities laws'. SPCX is squarely third-party: SpaceX's own final prospectus (424B4, 2026-06-12, CIK 0001181412) contains zero occurrences of 'tokeniz', 'Solana' or 'Backpack', so the issuer of the underlying has neither endorsed nor acknowledged these tokens.

British Virgin Islands law governs the Issuer Terms and Conditions, and 'all transactions contemplated herein are deemed to occur in the British Virgin Islands' (cl. 2.1). New York law (UCC Article 8, incl. s.8-110(e)) governs the separate OFF-CHAIN security entitlement held in a Backpack Securities account. BVI Electronic Transactions Act 2001 is invoked for electronic assignment of beneficial interests.

conclusions.label: How value can leave the wrapper
conclusions.conclusion: Deposit the token from a Solana wallet into a Backpack Exchange account; the token is burned and the position becomes a traditional securities holding (a UCC Article 8 security entitlement) in the same account. The trustee's mechanics are: lock the tokens, burn them, then either transfer the pro rata portion of the pooled shares or — at the trustee's determination — sell them and relay the net cash proceeds ('Redemption Relay', cl. 4.2(iii)-(iv), cl. 4.6), so share delivery is not guaranteed. Onward movement to an outside broker is described as 'ACATS- and DTCC-eligible via the brokerage infrastructure', but Backpack's own support docs state plainly that 'ACATS transfers to other brokerages are still being worked on and are not currently available' and 'Support for external broker-to-broker stock transfers is still under development and is not yet available'.

insolvency.headline: Insolvency outcome is not established.
insolvency.holderStanding: The token is, in the issuer's own words, 'a non-negotiable digital record evidencing a pro rata beneficial entitlement (if any)' as beneficiary of a BVI bare trust over a pooled holding of the referenced shares — with no entitlement to any specific identifiable share. Crucially, the trustee recognises only Trek Forge Ltd (a Backpack affiliate) as Tokenholder and sole beneficiary; a person holding the token in their own wallet 'becomes the on-chain holder of those Tokens for blockchain transfer purposes only' and has no redemption, distribution, instruction or enforcement right against the trust unless and until a 'Direct Redemption Contingency' occurs (Backpack insolvency, cessation, >90 days of suspended redemptions, court order, etc.) and the trustee expressly registers them. In practice a holder realises value by depositing the token back into a KYC'd Backpack Exchange account, which burns it and credits an off-chain UCC Article 8 security entitlement.

operationalDetails.omnibusOrCommingling: Real SpaceX shares are held through regulated US brokerage infrastructure in an OMNIBUS account at RQD Clearing, LLC (Clearing Broker; SEC-registered, FINRA & SIPC member, CRD 134284 / SEC 8-66826), with Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC as Intermediary Broker (CRD 317194 / SEC 8-70868).
operationalDetails.enforcementStanding: No separate enforcement representative is structured here; standing depends on the holder claim and governing terms reproduced above.

insolvency.caveat: A contractual label such as “segregated”, “trust” or “first priority” is not treated as a court-tested insolvency result unless the dossier records that authority.

corporateActions.actions: For the token: dividends received on the pool are applied by the trustee 'to the acquisition of additional units of such Approved Asset (net of any applicable fees, expenses, or withholdings)' (cl. 3.7), and Backpack describes this as automatic reinvestment into additional tokenized shares with corporate actions reflected through 'proportional token balance adjustments designed to maintain economic equivalence'. The mint carries the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension for exactly that, though its multiplier was still 1 on 2026-09-16 (SpaceX pays no dividend). Voting: cl. 3.9 has the trustee exercise voting only on instructions from the registered Tokenholder — i.e. Trek Forge — so an on-chain holder has no voting channel; and on the off-chain brokerage side Backpack's own status table lists voting rights, cash dividend payouts, and splits/corporate actions reflected in balances as all 'still being worked on', not enabled.
corporateActions.caveat: Economic equivalence may be delivered by cash, balance adjustment or issuer calculation; it is not assumed to reproduce the underlying shareholder right.

redemption.eligibility: Practically: any user with a KYC-verified Backpack Exchange account in a supported region (not US/UK/UAE/Japan, not Backpack EU) can deposit the token and have it converted into a traditional securities holding. Legally: only Trek Forge Ltd (or its nominee/custodian) may submit a redemption request to the trustee; 'on-chain holders and holders of Exchange Account Entitlements have no entitlement to access Redemption or burning functionalities in the ordinary course' (cl. 4.1(a)). Direct redemption against the trustee is available only after a Direct Redemption Contingency and then only subject to the trustee's KYC/KYT, proof of entitlement and express register update. No Prohibited Person or U.S. person may be registered as beneficiary or exercise redemption (cl. 4.1(c)).
redemption.rails: Deposit the token from a Solana wallet into a Backpack Exchange account; the token is burned and the position becomes a traditional securities holding (a UCC Article 8 security entitlement) in the same account. The trustee's mechanics are: lock the tokens, burn them, then either transfer the pro rata portion of the pooled shares or — at the trustee's determination — sell them and relay the net cash proceeds ('Redemption Relay', cl. 4.2(iii)-(iv), cl. 4.6), so share delivery is not guaranteed. Onward movement to an outside broker is described as 'ACATS- and DTCC-eligible via the brokerage infrastructure', but Backpack's own support docs state plainly that 'ACATS transfers to other brokerages are still being worked on and are not currently available' and 'Support for external broker-to-broker stock transfers is still under development and is not yet available'.
redemption.fees: Withdrawal of a tokenized security from Backpack Exchange to Solana: an estimated platform fee of approximately $0.50, paid in the tokenized security being withdrawn, with no additional fees. Deposits (token to traditional securities): no Backpack fee, holder pays the Solana network fee. Stock trading: no separate commission or platform fee; the quoted price is the traded price. Transaction Costs of a redemption are borne by the holder and netted from proceeds; the trustee may also set off amounts owing.
redemption.minimum: From Backpack's own asset API (https://api.backpack.exchange/api/v1/assets): minimumDeposit 0.004 SPCX, minimumWithdrawal 0.008 SPCX, withdrawalFee 0.004 SPCX. On the brokerage leg every stock order must be worth at least $1; fractional to 0.01 share during regular hours, whole shares only outside them.
redemption.evidenceLabel: A redemption process is documented, but no independently observed completed redemption is recorded.

openQuestions: RESOLVED as a negative, kept for the record: there is no SEC-registered or FINRA-member entity named 'Backpack Securities'. BrokerCheck and SEC IAPD return zero records for Backpack, Backpack Securities, Trek Labs, Trek Nexus and Trek Forge; EDGAR has no filings. The only US registrations in the group are the two third-party brokers (RQD, Atomic Vaults) and a FinCEN MSB for Trek Labs, Inc. (Delaware) — the MSB itself was not verified against FinCEN's registrant database.

Who operates Solana program FewRXXTzV2WwigvTQNsVanhEmCM9wzfNvoT1divNtbVH, whose PDAs hold the permanent-delegate, freeze, pause, metadata, hook and mint authorities, and who holds its single upgrade-authority key ERc1sdq7Lwb74kjuage5foTpavWKxdwXHUvqfg2JX5gz? The program is unidentified in every Backpack and Sunrise document, is unilaterally upgradeable, has no published audit, and carries no timelock or notice obligation (cl. 8.2: the Company 'may, but is not required to, provide notice'). A permanent delegate reachable through a unilaterally upgradeable program is the strongest possible authority on a Token-2022 mint.
Has the permanent delegate ever been exercised, and is any log of admin actions published? Nothing was found.

Is there any attestation, proof-of-reserve or auditor report tying the 43,248.128967 SPCX outstanding to SpaceX shares held? None was found. What is the actual share count in the pool, and where is it evidenced?

Where exactly does legal title to the shares sit? The Issuer T&C say Trek Nexus Markets Ltd is 'legal owner or holder of record' as bare trustee; Backpack's pages say custody is at RQD Clearing and Atomic Vault Securities. The account chain linking a BVI trustee to those US brokers is not documented, nor is which entity's name is on the account.

Is the declaration of trust dated 2026-06-06 (the 'Instrument') published anywhere? It is the document that actually creates the trust, it is cited as governing by both Backpack (Issuer T&C cl. 1.7) and Sunrise's own ToS, and it could not be found anywhere. Holders cannot read the instrument that defines their entitlement.

Terminology conflict inside Backpack's own materials: the tokenized-securities comparison table says the legal framework is a 'Claim on SPV holding the underlying assets', while the binding Issuer T&C describe a BVI bare trust, and the 'Real Ownership & Legal Framework' page boasts the product is 'not ... SPV interest'. Which characterisation does the issuer stand behind?

Backpack's docs spell the intermediary broker 'Atomic Vault Securities, LLC'; FINRA's registered name is 'Atomic Vaults Securities, LLC' (plural, formerly Olympus Mons Securities, LLC). A small inaccuracy, but it is in the one sentence holders are told to verify on BrokerCheck.

Has a Direct Redemption Contingency mechanism ever been tested, and what evidence of entitlement would the trustee accept from an on-chain holder? The Risk Disclosure says there is 'no guarantee... that the Company will accept your evidence of entitlement'.

When will ACATS/DTCC external transfers, cash dividends, corporate-action balance updates and voting actually go live? All four were still listed as 'being worked on' in docs updated around 2026-09-06, roughly three months after launch.

Does Backpack hold SPCX in Exchange Custody for users who never withdraw, and if so what is the split between exchange-held and self-custodied supply? That ratio determines how much of the 27,160 holder count actually has redemption rights.

Are the terms versioned? The Google Drive hosting means a silent amendment would leave no public trace, while cl. 2.4 binds every secondary acquirer to 'any amendments in effect at the time of such acquisition'.

SPCX the Nasdaq ticker and SPCX the Solana token share a symbol, and Jupiter also lists Ondo's SPCXon, Backed's SPCXx, Tessera's tSpaceX and leveraged Shift wrappers. Is there any issuer guidance to prevent holders from depositing the wrong SPCX-symbol token to Backpack? The docs warn holders to verify the contract address but the collision is structural.

fields.value: The holder owns the actual ordinary share of the listed company. The 2026-08-12 press release furnished on Form 6-K states: 'These tokens are issuer-sponsored and recorded at the registry level, giving holders direct share ownership and the same legal standing as conventional shareholders - not a synthetic position or third-party wrapper.' The 2026-05-05 release: 'shareholders can now hold BLSH ordinary shares as tokens on the Solana blockchain' and 'Bringing real ordinary shares onto a public blockchain, administered by an SEC-registered transfer agent, is the next step.' There is no SPV, nominee or receipt layer. But the same release also states plainly that 'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form' — so the claim is a registered share recorded on EQ's register, of which the token is the on-chain representation.

None interposed. The token is the share; the register is EQ's. Shareholders 'withdraw, hold, and return tokens through EQ's Shareholder Central portal', i.e. the token form is a withdrawal of the shareholder's own registered position into a whitelisted wallet. No custodian, depositary or trustee is named for the tokenized form. Key management for the mint/freeze/permanent-delegate keys is undisclosed (contrast Superstate, which names Turnkey).

links.label: Transfer and control

fields.value: program-mediated — Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified on-chain 2026-09-16), so every newly created BLSH token account is born frozen and unusable until the freeze authority (single wallet 4Be7JXd6JaiXd6KkSMBEya5yt19gq1d11NEWTZC6Bsgk) thaws it. The issuer describes the effect exactly: 'Transfers of onchain BLSH today move bilaterally between EQ-whitelisted wallet addresses; AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled. Any attempt to send BLSH tokens to a non-whitelisted address will fail at the smart-contract level, maintaining compliance with U.S. securities laws and anti-money-laundering rules.' Note a structural oddity: the mint carries an initialized TransferHook extension whose programId is null — the hook slot is reserved and its authority is the permanent-delegate wallet, but no hook program is set, so no per-transfer hook logic runs today. The gate is default-frozen accounts plus an off-chain-controlled freeze key, and the hook could be switched on later without redeploying the mint.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: Largely aspirational and entirely undocumented in operational terms. The 2026-05-05 release promises 'programmable corporate actions executed by smart contracts' as a possibility ('may open a set of possibilities'), not as a live feature. Dividends: Bullish has declared none on its ordinary shares, so there is no dividend path to test; no token dividend mechanism (cash, stablecoin or scrip) is described anywhere. Voting/proxy: a tokenized holder is a holder of record on EQ's register and should receive proxy materials through EQ's ordinary machinery, but no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented and there is no on-chain voting; no instance of a tokenized holder voting was found. Splits: the mint carries Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount with multiplier 1, so a split could be applied at the mint without reissuing tokens — never exercised. Emergency: the PausableConfig extension lets the authority halt all BLSH transfers in one instruction; no published policy governs when it would be used, who decides, or what holders are told. Lost/stolen shares: the PermanentDelegate makes recovery mechanically possible, but no recovery procedure is published (contrast Superstate, whose Terms §6.2 describe allowlist restrictions and recovery mechanisms).

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: Regulated US/Cayman/Gibraltar path with a documentary hole in the middle. The underlying security is the registered, NYSE-listed ordinary share of an SEC-reporting foreign private issuer. EQ is an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-00416). Bullish 'received approval from the GFSC to offer tokenized securities trading' in June 2026. The tokenization itself is disclosed to the SEC only by furnishing press releases on Form 6-K (2026-05-05 for the Equiniti merger, 2026-08-13 furnishing the 2026-08-12 tokenized-trading release); the tokenization is NOT described in the FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-03-10), which predates it and contains no mention of Equiniti (verified 2026-09-17: zero hits for 'equiniti' in the full document) or of tokenizing Bullish's own shares. The 20-F does, however, disclose the enabling registration twice - 'In December 2025, we registered with the SEC to operate as a transfer agent in the U.S.' (p. 45) and 'In December 2025, Bullish registered with the SEC as a transfer agent' (p. 49) - which is Bullish Digital TA LLC, SEC Transfer Agent File No. 084-07032, effective 2025-12-18, roughly five months before the launch. No risk-factor disclosure, no SEC no-action letter and no exemptive relief was located. The 2026-05-05 release carries only a generic caution that 'Tokenized securities are a novel instrument and there is limited legal, regulatory, judicial, operational and market precedent for their treatment.'

Cayman Islands companies law governs the ordinary shares and the share register; US federal securities law governs the listing and the transfer agent (Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21 apply to EQ); Gibraltar financial services law governs the exchange that lists the token. NO token-specific terms of service, token holder agreement or governing-law clause for the tokenized form was located — this is the single largest documentary gap relative to the Superstate peer, where the Transfer Agent & Terms of Service Agreement and the Digital Transfer Agency Agreement are both public.

The 2026-08-12 press release furnished on Form 6-K states: 'These tokens are issuer-sponsored and recorded at the registry level, giving holders direct share ownership and the same legal standing as conventional shareholders - not a synthetic position or third-party wrapper.' There is no SPV, nominee or receipt layer. But the same release also states plainly that 'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form' — so the claim is a registered share recorded on EQ's register, of which the token is the on-chain representation.

conclusions.label: How shareholder economics pass through
conclusions.conclusion: Largely aspirational and entirely undocumented in operational terms. The 2026-05-05 release promises 'programmable corporate actions executed by smart contracts' as a possibility ('may open a set of possibilities'), not as a live feature. Dividends: Bullish has declared none on its ordinary shares, so there is no dividend path to test; no token dividend mechanism (cash, stablecoin or scrip) is described anywhere. Voting/proxy: a tokenized holder is a holder of record on EQ's register and should receive proxy materials through EQ's ordinary machinery, but no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented and there is no on-chain voting; no instance of a tokenized holder voting was found. Splits: the mint carries Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount with multiplier 1, so a split could be applied at the mint without reissuing tokens — never exercised. Emergency: the PausableConfig extension lets the authority halt all BLSH transfers in one instruction; no published policy governs when it would be used, who decides, or what holders are told. Lost/stolen shares: the PermanentDelegate makes recovery mechanically possible, but no recovery procedure is published (contrast Superstate, whose Terms §6.2 describe allowlist restrictions and recovery mechanisms).

NO token-specific terms of service, token holder agreement or governing-law clause for the tokenized form was located — this is the single largest documentary gap relative to the Superstate peer, where the Transfer Agent & Terms of Service Agreement and the Digital Transfer Agency Agreement are both public.

eligibleHolders.name: allowlisted wallets
eligibleHolders.note: ‘Transfers of onchain BLSH today move bilaterally between EQ-whitelisted wallet addresses ... Any attempt to send BLSH tokens to a non-whitelisted address will fail at the smart-contract level.’ Enforced by defaultAccountState=Frozen; unlike Superstate there is no allowlist program, so the permitted set cannot be enumerated by anyone outside EQ.

eligibleHolders.name: KYC-verified platform users
eligibleHolders.note: Moving between book-entry and token form requires an EQ Shareholder Central account. No eligibility criteria, jurisdictional exclusions, street-name pathway, KYC provider or refusal process is published.

transfer.mechanism: program-mediated — Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified on-chain 2026-09-16), so every newly created BLSH token account is born frozen and unusable until the freeze authority (single wallet 4Be7JXd6JaiXd6KkSMBEya5yt19gq1d11NEWTZC6Bsgk) thaws it. The issuer describes the effect exactly: 'Transfers of onchain BLSH today move bilaterally between EQ-whitelisted wallet addresses; AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled. Any attempt to send BLSH tokens to a non-whitelisted address will fail at the smart-contract level, maintaining compliance with U.S. securities laws and anti-money-laundering rules.' Note a structural oddity: the mint carries an initialized TransferHook extension whose programId is null — the hook slot is reserved and its authority is the permanent-delegate wallet, but no hook program is set, so no per-transfer hook logic runs today. The gate is default-frozen accounts plus an off-chain-controlled freeze key, and the hook could be switched on later without redeploying the mint.

scope.distinction: A wallet may be technically able to receive a token while its owner is contractually ineligible, unable to redeem, or excluded from rights under the governing documents.

insolvency.headline: The holder claim is the registered share itself; transfer-agent and register continuity remain operational dependencies.
insolvency.holderStanding: The holder owns the actual ordinary share of the listed company. The 2026-08-12 press release furnished on Form 6-K states: 'These tokens are issuer-sponsored and recorded at the registry level, giving holders direct share ownership and the same legal standing as conventional shareholders - not a synthetic position or third-party wrapper.' The 2026-05-05 release: 'shareholders can now hold BLSH ordinary shares as tokens on the Solana blockchain' and 'Bringing real ordinary shares onto a public blockchain, administered by an SEC-registered transfer agent, is the next step.' There is no SPV, nominee or receipt layer. But the same release also states plainly that 'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form' — so the claim is a registered share recorded on EQ's register, of which the token is the on-chain representation.

operationalDetails.enforcementStanding: The person recognised on the official share register has shareholder standing; the token and transfer-agent process determine whether the wallet holder is that person.

insolvency.caveat: A contractual label such as “segregated”, “trust” or “first priority” is not treated as a court-tested insolvency result unless the dossier records that authority.

corporateActions.actions: Largely aspirational and entirely undocumented in operational terms. The 2026-05-05 release promises 'programmable corporate actions executed by smart contracts' as a possibility ('may open a set of possibilities'), not as a live feature. Dividends: Bullish has declared none on its ordinary shares, so there is no dividend path to test; no token dividend mechanism (cash, stablecoin or scrip) is described anywhere. Voting/proxy: a tokenized holder is a holder of record on EQ's register and should receive proxy materials through EQ's ordinary machinery, but no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented and there is no on-chain voting; no instance of a tokenized holder voting was found. Splits: the mint carries Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount with multiplier 1, so a split could be applied at the mint without reissuing tokens — never exercised. Emergency: the PausableConfig extension lets the authority halt all BLSH transfers in one instruction; no published policy governs when it would be used, who decides, or what holders are told. Lost/stolen shares: the PermanentDelegate makes recovery mechanically possible, but no recovery procedure is published (contrast Superstate, whose Terms §6.2 describe allowlist restrictions and recovery mechanisms).
corporateActions.caveat: Registration supports shareholder rights, but the operational channel for a token-held position must still be documented.

redemption.eligibility: Registered shareholders with an EQ Shareholder Central account. 'EQ maintains the official record of ownership whether shares are held in book-entry form or token form, and shareholders can move between the two through EQ's Shareholder Central portal.' Eligibility criteria, jurisdictional exclusions and whether non-US or non-registered (street-name) holders can participate are not published.
redemption.rails: Bidirectional conversion between book-entry and token form via EQ's Shareholder Central portal: 'Shareholders can withdraw, hold, and return tokens through EQ's Shareholder Central portal.' No on-chain burn address is published, no SLA or expected duration is stated, and no cash payout results from returning tokens — the shareholder gets a book-entry position, which must then be sold through a broker on NYSE, or the token sold on Bullish Exchange.
redemption.fees: unknown — no fee schedule for tokenization, de-tokenization or wallet whitelisting was located.
redemption.evidenceLabel: A redemption process is documented, but no independently observed completed redemption is recorded.

openQuestions: WHERE ARE THE TERMS? No token terms of service, holder agreement, transfer agency agreement, technical documentation, allowlist policy, fee schedule or audit for onchain BLSH could be found — the entire public record is two press releases. Every question below exists because of this. The Superstate peer's equivalent documents are public (one of them as an SEC exhibit), so a direct request to Bullish IR for the EQ Shareholder Central tokenization terms is the single highest-value next step.

Which register controls in a dispute? The launch release both assigns the official record to EQ and claims 'a single authoritative ledger'. If the chain and EQ's register disagree — after a pause, a forced burn, or a synchronisation failure — no located document says which wins or who bears the loss.

Who holds the keys, Bullish or Equiniti? 4Be7JXd6... (mint + freeze) and DPT54eBQ... (permanent delegate, pause, hook, split, metadata, confidential transfer) are plain single-signer wallets with no multisig program account and no disclosed custodian. Whether the transfer agent or the issuer can freeze and claw back a shareholder's position is unresolved, and it is exactly the question the SEC transfer-agent rules would care about.

What is the real shareholder-level adoption? 151,810,063.5 tokens across 21 Token-2022 accounts. How much of that is a single DTC/Cede & Co. position or an EQ omnibus account, how many accounts are genuine shareholder self-custody wallets, and how many distinct shareholders have ever used Shareholder Central to withdraw? Without this, 'fully tokenized cap table' cannot be converted into a maturity signal. getTokenLargestAccounts on the mint was rate-limited (HTTP 429) on the public RPC on 2026-09-16 and should be retried against a paid endpoint — it would answer this in one call.

Why is a TransferHook extension initialized with programId null? The hook slot is reserved and its authority is the permanent-delegate wallet. Is a hook program planned (which would move compliance on-chain and make the perimeter auditable, a genuine upgrade), or is this an artefact of the mint-creation tooling? Either way a hook can be attached later with no notice.

Why is ConfidentialTransferMint configured at all, with autoApproveNewAccounts false and a null auditor ElGamal key? Confidential transfers on a security whose transfer agent must maintain a holder register is a strange combination. If confidential transfers were enabled with no auditor key, balances would be opaque to everyone including the transfer agent. Not enabled today; the configuration is unexplained.

When does the tokenization reach a risk factor? The FY2025 20-F (filed 2026-03-10) predates the launch and does not mention it. The FY2026 20-F, due around March 2027, is the first filing that must address tokenized BLSH in Item 3.D — and the Superstate issuers' disclosures ('no current trading venues', conversion 'could take up to multiple weeks', 'pricing discrepancies ... may be substantial') are the benchmark for what candid disclosure looks like.
What is the conversion latency between token form and NYSE-tradeable book-entry form? This is the number that bounds the basis between Bullish Exchange and NYSE. Unpublished.

What happens to the independence of the stack when the Equiniti acquisition closes (expected Q1 2027)? Today EQ is an independent SEC-registered transfer agent — the only outside party in the structure and the basis for much of what scores well here. Post-closing, issuer, transfer agent, tokenization infrastructure and trading venue are one group holding freeze, claw-back and pause keys over its own shareholders. Note also that the deal is not certain: the merger agreement can terminate if not consummated by 2027-02-04 (extendable to 2027-05-04 and 2027-08-04).

Is the tokenized form the same security identifier as the NYSE-listed share? No CUSIP or ISIN is published for either form and the token metadata carries none, so the same-class claim rests on the issuer's word plus the supply arithmetic. The Superstate peer's published CUSIPs are the sharpest wrapper-versus-share discriminator available and Bullish supplies no equivalent.

How do dividends, proxy voting and splits actually work for a token holder? Bullish pays no dividend, so the path is untested; ScaledUiAmount sits at multiplier 1, so no split has occurred; and 'programmable corporate actions executed by smart contracts' is offered as a possibility, not a mechanism. No tokenized holder is known to have voted.

Is there any recovery procedure for lost keys or stolen tokens? The PermanentDelegate makes it mechanically possible and the release warns of 'risks related to the loss of private keys and wallet access' without offering any remedy. Whether EQ will restore a position, and on what evidence, is unpublished — and under Rule 17Ad-17 EQ has lost-securityholder obligations that sit oddly with an unrecoverable self-custodied token.

Can non-US holders, and holders in street name rather than on the register, obtain tokens at all? The whitelist rationale cites US securities and AML law; no eligibility matrix, jurisdictional exclusion list or street-name pathway is published. A NYSE-listed Cayman issuer with a global shareholder base makes this a live question.

links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: The holder owns an unsecured-in-form but collateral-secured debt claim on Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited — a blockchain-based tracker certificate / structured note whose redemption amount tracks the total return of the referenced share or ETF. The holder has a put option to redeem for cash/stablecoin at the tracked value, plus the benefit of a first-priority perfected security interest in the collateral held by Ankura Trust Company as Security Agent; the holder has no shareholder voting or information rights. Physical delivery of the underlying is excluded under the Sales Terms and no party may demand conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities — with one documented exception outside the Sales Terms: authorized participants with a linked Alpaca brokerage account can redeem Ondo Stocks for the underlying securities through Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network (ITN) on Ethereum and BNB Chain.

Alpaca Securities LLC (SEC-registered, FINRA member broker-dealer; New York) holds the equities/ETFs through the DTC indirect holding system and provides the trading/clearing accounts. BitGo Trust Company, Inc. (Sioux Falls, SD) holds fiat and stablecoins/tokens. The 2026-09-10 Ankura report also names SVB, Coinbase, Circle, Anchorage and a 'Bridge Account' and 'PSM' as holding locations for cash/stablecoins.

links.label: Issuance and redemption

fields.value: Only 'Onboarded Purchasers' who have completed the issuer's full KYC and satisfy the eligibility criteria (non-US person, not a Prohibited Person, and in several jurisdictions professional/accredited-investor status). KYC is an express condition precedent to redemption, so a secondary-market buyer may hold a token it cannot redeem. Onboarding was institutional-only at the time of the Solana launch, with retail 'coming soon'.

On-chain atomic mint/redeem against USDon (the platform stablecoin), with USDC atomically swapped 1:1 to/from USDon via a stablecoin swapper (users are not whitelisted for that swap by default). Requires an off-chain signed attestation (secp256k1) from the Ondo GM API quoting price and amount, submitted to the on-chain program by a whitelisted address. For an ordinary Onboarded Purchaser redemption is for cash/stablecoin only, and the Sales Terms exclude physical delivery and bar any conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities. Separately, Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network lets authorized participants mint from, and redeem into, the underlying securities in a linked Alpaca brokerage account on Ethereum and BNB Chain (no Ondo fee for ITN mint/redeem). Bank wire redemption not supported.

Sales Terms define Purchaser Fees owed to the Issuer for issuance AND redemption of up to 0.1% of the market price of the Underlyings; no separate redemption fee is advertised in the docs, and Ondo also retains the spread between the quoted token price and the price at which it trades the underlying. Ondo charges no fee for mint/redeem through Alpaca's ITN channel. Investor pays gas. Dividends are reinvested net of 30% US withholding tax on the BVI issuer.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: Voting: since 2026-04-28, via a Broadridge integration, tokenholders can express non-binding voting PREFERENCES to the issuer regarding the shares the issuer beneficially owns; the issuer has no legal obligation to follow them, and the holder has no shareholder voting right. Dividends are reinvested into the referenced stock net of withholding tax and expressed as an increase in the 'shares per token' multiplier; on Solana this is surfaced through the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension, so the displayed balance grows rather than the price (NVDAon multiplier 1.0017152487959897, AAPLon 1.003376073740221, SPYon 1.0077209101501272, TSLAon 1.0 as read on-chain 2026-09-16). Stock splits are handled the same way. Trading is paused around ex-dividend dates (roughly 7:50-8:10pm ET the day before the ex-date) and halted for ETF distributions until the amount is known; assets enter a reduced-size 'limited' state around earnings. Halts are listed at status.ondo.finance. The issuer may replace the Underlying held as collateral, and may exercise an Issuer Call Option to terminate and redeem all (not part) of a token series after a Termination Notice.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: Not a registered US offering. Tokens sold only outside the US under Regulation S; issuer not registered as an investment company under the 1940 Act. EU-facing: Base Prospectus for a 'Program for the issuance of tokenized Securities' approved by the Liechtenstein Financial Markets Authority on 11.11.2025 (valid to 11.11.2026), with per-asset Final Terms filed with the FMA and PRIIPs Key Information Documents; NVDAon carries ISIN VGG7001AAH73. Some assets carry an 'Admission to Trading Notice on Binance MTF in Abu Dhabi Global Market'. Ondo Finance Inc. filed a no-action request with SEC Trading & Markets on 2026-04-13 to tokenize the DTC security entitlements that collateralise OGM products (via its SEC-registered transfer agent Oasis Pro TA, LLC) — that request does not cover issuance of the OGM tokens themselves.

Swiss law governs the form/transfer/cancellation of the tokens as Ledger-Based Securities under arts. 973d et seqq. CO, and governs the Sales Terms (arbitration: Swiss Rules, seat Zurich, English). Collateral Agreement and Alpaca account control agreement: New York law. BitGo account control agreement: South Dakota law. Administrative Services Agreement: Delaware law. Base Prospectus approved under EU Prospectus Regulation by the Liechtenstein FMA.

conclusions.label: How shareholder economics pass through
conclusions.conclusion: Voting: since 2026-04-28, via a Broadridge integration, tokenholders can express non-binding voting PREFERENCES to the issuer regarding the shares the issuer beneficially owns; the issuer has no legal obligation to follow them, and the holder has no shareholder voting right. Dividends are reinvested into the referenced stock net of withholding tax and expressed as an increase in the 'shares per token' multiplier; on Solana this is surfaced through the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension, so the displayed balance grows rather than the price (NVDAon multiplier 1.0017152487959897, AAPLon 1.003376073740221, SPYon 1.0077209101501272, TSLAon 1.0 as read on-chain 2026-09-16). Stock splits are handled the same way. Trading is paused around ex-dividend dates (roughly 7:50-8:10pm ET the day before the ex-date) and halted for ETF distributions until the amount is known; assets enter a reduced-size 'limited' state around earnings. Halts are listed at status.ondo.finance. The issuer may replace the Underlying held as collateral, and may exercise an Issuer Call Option to terminate and redeem all (not part) of a token series after a Termination Notice.

conflicts.note: CORRECTION: the dossier said the holder has 'no right ever to demand delivery of the actual shares'. That is the Sales Terms position (p. 74, p. 108, p. 111) and remains true for an ordinary Onboarded Purchaser, but Ondo documents an in-kind channel: authorized participants with a linked Alpaca brokerage account can redeem Ondo Stocks for the underlying securities on Ethereum and BNB Chain. holderClaim now says so.

CORRECTION: the dossier implied a next-day report ('due to the issuer by 4:30pm GMT on the next calendar day after the Issuer Report Day'). The full chain is longer: the Issuer's data is due on the THIRD business day after the Calculation Day, and only then is Ankura's report due by 4:30 pm GMT the next calendar day — so a publication lag of several business days is what the contract provides for, not a lapse.

CORRECTION: the dossier said redemption is 'for cash/stablecoin only — never for the underlying shares'. True of the Sales Terms put option, but Ondo's own docs describe an in-kind redemption for authorized participants on Ethereum and BNB Chain that delivers the underlying shares into a linked Alpaca account (no Ondo fee). redemption.rails now records both paths.

CORRECTION: the dossier said 'No explicit redemption fee'. The Sales Terms define a contractual Purchaser Fee of up to 0.1% of the market price of the Underlyings, owed for issuance AND redemption. The field now states the 0.1% cap alongside the retained spread.

insolvency.headline: The holder relies on a security package and its perfection, priority, collateral scope and enforcement machinery—not direct ownership of the shares.

securityInterest.holder: Ankura Trust Company, LLC as Security Agent, for the benefit of the Secured Parties (tokenholders)

insolvency.holderStanding: The holder owns an unsecured-in-form but collateral-secured debt claim on Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited — a blockchain-based tracker certificate / structured note whose redemption amount tracks the total return of the referenced share or ETF. The holder has a put option to redeem for cash/stablecoin at the tracked value, plus the benefit of a first-priority perfected security interest in the collateral held by Ankura Trust Company as Security Agent; the holder has no shareholder voting or information rights. Physical delivery of the underlying is excluded under the Sales Terms and no party may demand conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities — with one documented exception outside the Sales Terms: authorized participants with a linked Alpaca brokerage account can redeem Ondo Stocks for the underlying securities through Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network (ITN) on Ethereum and BNB Chain.

operationalDetails.perfectionOrPriority: The holder has a put option to redeem for cash/stablecoin at the tracked value, plus the benefit of a first-priority perfected security interest in the collateral held by Ankura Trust Company as Security Agent; the holder has no shareholder voting or information rights.
operationalDetails.enforcementStanding: Ankura Trust Company, LLC as Security Agent, for the benefit of the Secured Parties (tokenholders) is the recorded security holder or enforcement representative; the tokenholder depends on that agent and the operative security documents.

insolvency.caveat: A contractual label such as “segregated”, “trust” or “first priority” is not treated as a court-tested insolvency result unless the dossier records that authority.

corporateActions.actions: Voting: since 2026-04-28, via a Broadridge integration, tokenholders can express non-binding voting PREFERENCES to the issuer regarding the shares the issuer beneficially owns; the issuer has no legal obligation to follow them, and the holder has no shareholder voting right. Dividends are reinvested into the referenced stock net of withholding tax and expressed as an increase in the 'shares per token' multiplier; on Solana this is surfaced through the Token-2022 ScaledUiAmount extension, so the displayed balance grows rather than the price (NVDAon multiplier 1.0017152487959897, AAPLon 1.003376073740221, SPYon 1.0077209101501272, TSLAon 1.0 as read on-chain 2026-09-16). Stock splits are handled the same way. Trading is paused around ex-dividend dates (roughly 7:50-8:10pm ET the day before the ex-date) and halted for ETF distributions until the amount is known; assets enter a reduced-size 'limited' state around earnings. Halts are listed at status.ondo.finance. The issuer may replace the Underlying held as collateral, and may exercise an Issuer Call Option to terminate and redeem all (not part) of a token series after a Termination Notice.
corporateActions.caveat: Economic equivalence may be delivered by cash, balance adjustment or issuer calculation; it is not assumed to reproduce the underlying shareholder right.

redemption.eligibility: Only 'Onboarded Purchasers' who have completed the issuer's full KYC and satisfy the eligibility criteria (non-US person, not a Prohibited Person, and in several jurisdictions professional/accredited-investor status). KYC is an express condition precedent to redemption, so a secondary-market buyer may hold a token it cannot redeem. Onboarding was institutional-only at the time of the Solana launch, with retail 'coming soon'.
redemption.rails: On-chain atomic mint/redeem against USDon (the platform stablecoin), with USDC atomically swapped 1:1 to/from USDon via a stablecoin swapper (users are not whitelisted for that swap by default). Requires an off-chain signed attestation (secp256k1) from the Ondo GM API quoting price and amount, submitted to the on-chain program by a whitelisted address. For an ordinary Onboarded Purchaser redemption is for cash/stablecoin only, and the Sales Terms exclude physical delivery and bar any conversion into certificated, uncertificated or book-entry securities. Separately, Alpaca's Instant Tokenization Network lets authorized participants mint from, and redeem into, the underlying securities in a linked Alpaca brokerage account on Ethereum and BNB Chain (no Ondo fee for ITN mint/redeem). Bank wire redemption not supported.
redemption.fees: Sales Terms define Purchaser Fees owed to the Issuer for issuance AND redemption of up to 0.1% of the market price of the Underlyings; no separate redemption fee is advertised in the docs, and Ondo also retains the spread between the quoted token price and the price at which it trades the underlying. Ondo charges no fee for mint/redeem through Alpaca's ITN channel. Investor pays gas. Dividends are reinvested net of 30% US withholding tax on the BVI issuer.
redemption.evidenceLabel: A redemption process is documented, but no independently observed completed redemption is recorded.

openQuestions: What is the numeric overcollateralisation factor for 'Other Collateral' per asset type? The Sales Terms say it is defined therein and varies, but the value was not located in the public text, and the daily report gives only a pooled Asset-to-Obligation Ratio (108.02% on 2026-09-10).

How much of the collateral is actually the underlying shares versus permitted substitutes (cash, unlisted instruments, crypto assets)? The daily report shows a large stablecoin and cash component (~$66m USDC/USDT plus ~$35m Alpaca cash) but does not label any of it as Standard vs Other Collateral for a given series.

Why are the Ankura reports not published at https://ondo.finance/global-markets as Sales Terms s.8.1(b) requires, and is the Dropbox folder considered contractual compliance? Also: is the 2-4 business day publication lag a process issue or a change in practice?

Will a TransferHook program be installed on the Solana mints, and if so what will it enforce? The hook authority is set and press describes hooks as the compliance mechanism, but programId is null today — installing one would silently convert unconditionalTransfers from yes to no.

Who controls the freeze authority key 51QVCuHfL1FeNjd8BDeffCKhCcAYoULnVB3yjNhShiuK and the mint/scaled-UI/pause authority 9foMHsSDq7nMg4WPusSz9eY7tyxyukqborA8GyU5cUxD — single signer or multisig, and with what timelock? The Solana program README describes role-based access control but the on-chain authorities were not resolved to multisigs.

The NVDAon Final Terms (11.11.2025) name Ethereum Mainnet only as the Blockchain. Have FMA-filed Final Terms been supplemented to cover the Solana issuance (Jan 2026), and does the Base Prospectus Supplement of 04.05.2026 do that?
Are the Spearbit and Cyfrin audit reports published, dated, and do they cover the Solana Anchor program (github.com/ondoprotocol/global-markets-solana) rather than only the EVM contracts?
Is there an annual audited financial statement for Ondo Global Markets (BVI) Limited? The docs promise annual independent audits 'made available to investors' but none was found published.

Practical effect of the Prohibited-Persons clause: a secondary buyer can receive the token but 'shall have no rights under any Offering Documents'. Does the issuer track and act on this, and how would it treat a chain of transfers through an ineligible holder?
The 2026-04-13 SEC no-action request would put the collateral security entitlements on Ethereum via Oasis Pro TA. Has the SEC responded, and would that change the OGM holder's claim?

Broadridge voting-preference passthrough (live 2026-04-28): does it require KYC/onboarding, a minimum holding, or an Ondo account, and is it available to Solana holders? The issuer's discretion to disregard preferences is not quantified or reported on.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: Unlicensed and self-disclaiming. Site disclaimer: "PreStocks is not a broker-dealer, investment advisor, exchange operator, transfer agent, custodian, virtual asset service provider, or similar regulated entity." No securities registration or exemption is cited; the ToS instead asserts "All blockchain transfers via the Services are secondary transfers effected outside the United States and are not primary offerings to U.S. persons" (Regulation S-style posture, but Reg S is never named).

British Virgin Islands law. ToS s.“Governing Law and Jurisdiction”: all matters and disputes "shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the British Virgin Islands". Note the BVI is simultaneously on the Prohibited Jurisdictions list. Disputes go to good-faith negotiation for 30 days, then binding arbitration under the London Court of International Arbitration Rules; seat London, England; sole arbitrator; English language; individual basis only (no class actions), with the courts of the British Virgin Islands taking exclusive jurisdiction over any claim for which the class-action waiver is held unenforceable. What is still missing is the counterparty, not the law: no issuing entity or jurisdiction of incorporation is named.

scope.distinction: A wallet may be technically able to receive a token while its owner is contractually ineligible, unable to redeem, or excluded from rights under the governing documents.

insolvency.headline: Insolvency outcome is not established.
insolvency.holderStanding: A bearer Token-2022 token that "reference[s] economic exposure to designated pre-IPO companies" and confers "no ownership, voting, dividend, information, or other legal rights". The ToS grants no proprietary interest in any SPV, share or asset; the holder's only stated entitlement is to request redemption for USDC "or another mutually agreed form of value", which the operator may satisfy instead by pointing the holder at on-chain liquidity.

operationalDetails.enforcementStanding: No separate enforcement representative is structured here; standing depends on the holder claim and governing terms reproduced above.

insolvency.caveat: A contractual label such as “segregated”, “trust” or “first priority” is not treated as a court-tested insolvency result unless the dossier records that authority.

corporateActions.actions: IPO: underlying positions become convertible on-chain (without KYC) into an equivalent tokenized public stock; typical 6-month post-IPO lockup during which the token may trade at a discount; holders have 9 months post-IPO (3 months after lockup) to convert, after which "the tokens will expire worthless and will no longer be supported". M&A: cash deals distribute net proceeds pro rata as USDC; equity deals may become convertible into a tokenized version of the acquirer's equity "if we create and support one", with a 6-month conversion window, then expiry. Separately, balances can be restated unilaterally through the scaledUiAmountConfig multiplier, and this has happened twice: SPACEX x5 effective 2026-06-10T04:30:00Z and OPENAI x1.4861347 effective 2026-07-17T16:30:00Z. Neither was explained publicly.
corporateActions.caveat: Economic equivalence may be delivered by cash, balance adjustment or issuer calculation; it is not assumed to reproduce the underlying shareholder right.

redemption.eligibility: Any non-US, non-Restricted holder "may request redemption" - discretionary, not an entitlement. Which path is used "depends on those circumstances"; the operator may direct the holder to on-chain liquidity instead of processing a redemption.
redemption.rails: USDC or "another mutually agreed form of value"; alternatively realisation via on-chain liquidity, conversions, wraps, migrations or exchanges. Post-IPO the stated path is conversion into an equivalent tokenized public stock rather than cash.
redemption.fees: Unbounded and unilateral. ToS reserves redemption, settlement, conversion and withdrawal fees plus markups/spreads, enforced "at the token, smart-contract, or program level" via transfer-fee configurations and hooks, changeable "without prior notice and without your consent", with no obligation "to publish, itemize, or explain the basis of any fee". Observed on-chain: 50 bps transfer fee, raised from 0 bps (fee epoch 848 -> 1032).
redemption.evidenceLabel: A redemption process is documented, but no independently observed completed redemption is recorded.

openQuestions: Who actually issues the tokens? No legal entity is named anywhere; "a distributed network of contributors" is not a counterparty a holder could sue, and the LCIA clause names no respondent.
Which holding entities hold the exposure, and in what form? Names are withheld as policy, so the 1:1 backing claim in the API description is unverifiable in principle, not just in practice.
Is ANTHROPIC exposure backed at all after Anthropic declared SPV transfers void under its transfer restrictions? The token still trades and the supply was never reduced.
Has any attestation report ever been produced to any holder on request, and at what cost?
Why was the OPENAI scaledUiAmount multiplier set to 1.4861347 on 2026-07-17 - a share split at OpenAI, a restatement of units per token, or a correction of over/under-collateralisation?

RESOLVED, kept for the record: the ToS last updated 2026-09-08 does elect a substantive law - the internal laws of the British Virgin Islands - with LCIA arbitration seated in London and BVI courts as the fallback forum. The BVI is also a Prohibited Jurisdiction under the same document. What remains unanswered is who the BVI-law counterparty is.
Why does SPACEX trade about 21% below the issuer's own mark if mint/redeem arbitrage works as the FAQ describes?
xAI has a live product page in sitemap.xml but no API entry or mint - is it unlaunched, delisted, or was it withdrawn?

The issuer's own press release adds that this is an 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE' and that 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Holders may move between forms: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. There is no SPV, receipt or nominee layer in the legal structure — but access runs through a broker-dealer's onboarding, so whether the holder is a registered holder of record in their own name or a customer of the broker-dealer is NOT established by any document located, and this is the central unresolved question for this issuer.

No custodian is interposed for the security itself — the token is the share and the register is Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC's master securityholder file. For its own corporate digital assets Securitize discloses self-custody via Fireblocks MPC ('enables us to retain exclusive control over the authorization of transactions without ever generating or storing a traditional private key'), and states that 'In the case of Securitize-issued tokenized securities held in self-custody utilizing Fireblocks infrastructure, Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent.' Investor-side custody may be self-custody (see transferRestrictions) or broker/custodian-held; the split is not disclosed.

fields.value: program-mediated, per-token whitelist. On-chain: Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so every new SECZ token account is frozen at birth and only the freeze authority (8Twerer..., an apparent program PDA) can thaw it; plus PausableConfig for a global halt. Off-chain: the Securitize Connect API documents wallet whitelisting scoped to a specific token ('adds a wallet address to the whitelist of an specific token', requiring a tokenId, since 'in a given domain there may be multiple tokens'), with wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and a 'not-authorised' response state. Notably the whitelist is NOT tied to a platform-hosted wallet: 'This is not required, as the whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' — a self-custodied address can be whitelisted directly. Contractually: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche holdings carry business-combination lock-ups. US persons are the TARGET market here ('eligible U.S. investors'), which inverts the usual tokenized-equity geofence.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: Securitize markets corporate-action servicing as a core transfer-agent capability — the S-1 describes 'a comprehensive suite of securities services including real-time approval, record-keeping, distributions, dividend issuances and compliance solutions' — so the institutional machinery genuinely exists and is exercised for third-party issuers (BUIDL and others). For SECZ specifically nothing has been exercised: Securitize Corp. declares no dividend, so the distribution path is untested on its own stock; the mint's ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, so no split has occurred; and no tokenized-holder proxy process or on-chain voting is documented. Two mechanisms are disclosed that are unusual and material. (1) FORK POLICY: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities' — a rare, explicit, pre-agreed chain-exception policy, and simultaneously a statement that the issuer, not the chain, decides. It adds that it 'would generally expect to follow the fork recognized by principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' and that 'In extreme circumstances, Securitize may determine that migrating assets to an alternative fork is necessary'. (2) MANUAL FALLBACK: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent' — an explicit off-chain recovery path that exists precisely because the chain is not the record. Emergency halt: PausableConfig on the mint, with no published policy for its use.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: The most heavily regulated of the three Solana-native issuers examined, and the only one where the tokenization vendor is itself the registrant. The underlying security is registered common stock of a Delaware SEC-reporting company listed on the NYSE (S-4 registration statement effective 2026-06-05; S-1 filed 2026-07-31, EFFECT 2026-08-07; 424B3 prospectuses 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-13). Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC is an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638). The S-1 describes the group as 'the only vertically integrated tokenization provider with SEC-registered entities across a transfer agent, broker-dealer, alternative trading system (ATS), investor advisor and fund administration'. Access to the tokenized form is intermediated by a regulated broker-dealer: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer' (note: the S-1 renders the entity name as 'Securities Markets, LLC'. RESOLVED 2026-09-17 against a primary source: Securitize's own 2026-07-02 press release names 'Securitize Markets, LLC, an SEC-registered broker-dealer and member FINRA/SIPC that operates an SEC-regulated Alternative Trading System (ATS)', so the S-1 wording is a typographical error in a registration statement and the gatekeeping broker-dealer is Securitize Markets, LLC). No exemptive relief or no-action letter for the tokenized form was located; the S-1 warns that 'market intermediaries may face unclear or evolving obligations'.

Delaware General Corporation Law governs the common stock and the share register; US federal securities law governs the listing, the transfer agent (Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21) and the broker-dealer/ATS gating access. No separate token terms of service or holder agreement for Tokenized SECZ was located; the operative public instrument is the Form S-1 prospectus risk factor plus the Securitize platform's general investor terms (not located in tokenized-SECZ-specific form).

conclusions.label: How shareholder economics pass through
conclusions.conclusion: Securitize markets corporate-action servicing as a core transfer-agent capability — the S-1 describes 'a comprehensive suite of securities services including real-time approval, record-keeping, distributions, dividend issuances and compliance solutions' — so the institutional machinery genuinely exists and is exercised for third-party issuers (BUIDL and others). For SECZ specifically nothing has been exercised: Securitize Corp. declares no dividend, so the distribution path is untested on its own stock; the mint's ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, so no split has occurred; and no tokenized-holder proxy process or on-chain voting is documented. Two mechanisms are disclosed that are unusual and material. (1) FORK POLICY: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities' — a rare, explicit, pre-agreed chain-exception policy, and simultaneously a statement that the issuer, not the chain, decides. It adds that it 'would generally expect to follow the fork recognized by principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' and that 'In extreme circumstances, Securitize may determine that migrating assets to an alternative fork is necessary'. (2) MANUAL FALLBACK: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent' — an explicit off-chain recovery path that exists precisely because the chain is not the record. No burn address, no processing time, no fee schedule and no step-by-step process was located in any public document. Because the transfer agent and the platform are the same group, the switch is an internal book movement rather than a coordination between two agents — mechanically simpler than the Superstate peer's DRS route, but also entirely un-auditable from outside.
redemption.evidenceLabel: A redemption process is documented, but no independently observed completed redemption is recorded.

openQuestions: MINT ATTRIBUTION IS INFERRED, NOT PUBLISHED. Securitize has published no Solana contract address anywhere located. 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED is attributed on the strength of its TokenMetadata URI pointing at metadata.securitize.io, matching name/symbol, the Token-2022 compliance extension set, a 2026-06-29 creation date (three days before listing) and a registry verified flag. That is strong circumstantial evidence, not issuer confirmation. Given four SECZ-branded impersonation mints on Solana, the single highest-value next step is asking Securitize IR to publish canonical addresses. Treat the address as high-confidence-but-unconfirmed until then.

Where is the $295M? Press reports $295M of tokenized SECZ; the Solana mint holds 148,998 tokens (~$1.24M). The S-1 puts locked-up business-combination shares on Avalanche, so the balance is presumably there — but Securitize publishes no per-chain supply figures and nothing reconciles the headline to the chains. The Avalanche contract address should be identified and its supply read to close this.

Is a tokenized holder a holder of record in their own name, or a customer position behind the group's broker-dealer? This is the most consequential unanswered question for grading, and it determines whether titleDeed really behaves like the Superstate peer's (where the holder's name, address and TIN sit on the register). Access runs through 'the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer', which is the shape of a customer relationship — yet the whitelisting API explicitly supports addresses with no Securitize iD profile, which is the shape of direct registration. Both cannot be the general case.

What is the correct name of the gatekeeping broker-dealer? The S-1 says 'Securities Markets, LLC'; Securitize's broker-dealer is publicly known as Securitize Markets, LLC. Most likely a typo in a registration statement, but it is the entity that controls who may hold the security, and it should be confirmed against the FINRA/SEC BD registration rather than assumed.

Which entity holds the on-chain authorities, and under what program? 8Twerer... (mint + freeze) is an apparent PDA whose owning program was not identified; D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA... (permanent delegate, pause, split, metadata) was not resolved at all. Whether these sit with Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC (the regulated registrar) or with an operating affiliate matters legally, and whether the program has a timelock or multisig gate matters for grading. Fireblocks MPC is disclosed for corporate treasury only.

What are the 117 token accounts? 148,998 tokens across 117 accounts, with Jupiter reporting 44 holders and a top-holders concentration of ~11.7%. How many are investor self-custody wallets versus platform/custodian/liquidity-pool accounts is unknown. getTokenLargestAccounts on the public RPC returned HTTP 429 on 2026-09-16 and should be retried against a paid endpoint.

Who are the 'on-chain liquidity provision partners' on Solana? The S-1 says Solana trading 'is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners' without naming them. Since holding SECZ requires whitelisting, a liquidity pool must itself be whitelisted — so the pool addresses, and whether pool LPs must be onboarded, are open. Jupiter reported zero volume in the 24h to 2026-09-16.

Is SECZ actually live as DeFi collateral? Press of 2026-08-20 reports SECZ linked to Solana on-chain credit markets. Unverified by rwa-sonar. If true it would need an oracle feed (none located) and would raise the same jurisdiction-of-use question the Superstate/Kamino integration raises.

Has the fork policy ever been applied, and who bears the loss? The S-1's fork provisions are the most developed chain-exception policy in this universe, but they allocate authority without allocating loss: nothing states what happens to a holder whose tokens end up on the chain Securitize does not recognise, or who compensates them. Also note the dependency it creates — the tie-break heuristic is whichever fork 'principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' recognise.

How do dividends, proxy voting and splits work for a tokenized holder? Securitize sells 'distributions, dividend issuances' as transfer-agent services and runs them for third-party issuers, but Securitize Corp. pays no dividend, the ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, and no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented. Untested on its own stock. Note the earnout structure (VWAP thresholds of $15/$20/$25 triggering Securitize Earnout Shares over five years from Closing) will cause share issuance that must propagate to the mint — a live, dated test of the control-book-to-chain path.
What is the token-to-nontokenized switch latency and fee? Unpublished, and it is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies.

Has the Solana token program been independently audited? Nothing public ties an audit to this deployment, despite Securitize's scale (BUIDL alone was >60% of its tokenized AUM at 2025-09-30) and its 21-chain integration.

links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: On paper: a membership interest in a designated Series of SHIFT DAO LLC whose sole purpose is to "acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to" one named index or stock. The Series 17 agreement says "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 says "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", with no voting, management or fiduciary rights. In practice three things break that chain. (1) The issuer's own site-wide legal notice says the opposite: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." (2) The executed Series agreements do not identify the token they govern - membership is obtained by holding a token "created from and constricted by the parameters defined in the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined" - so no published document links the SPL mint that trades on Jupiter to the Series whose treasury holds the asset; the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement compounds this by requiring "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". (3) What the Series is documented to hold is not the referenced equity but a daily-reset leveraged ETF share (Series 17: SPXL, Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3x, ISIN US25459W8626; Series 12: Direxion Daily TSLA X2, ISIN US25460G2865), so exposure to Tesla or the S&P 500 is delivered through a third party's derivative fund. Graded as derivative for that reason; if the Series agreements' "owners in the Series Assets" language controlled and were bound to these mints, the record would move to spv-claim-redeemable.

Two custodians are named, in the Risk Disclosure only: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets." The Collateral & Custody page adds that backing is held "with FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners" in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" and "off-balance-sheet". Marketing and press name Alpaca Markets as the brokerage rail. The holding entity itself is not named ("a private entity that holds the backing assets"), nor is the market maker that operates the B2B mint/burn endpoints, and no account, statement, holdings report or balance for any Series has been published.
